prompt:
Build `vcfcreds`, a stdlib-only Python 3.10+ package in this repository that inventories every credential SDDC Manager knows about. `python3 -m vcfcreds` is the entry point:

    python3 -m vcfcreds --base-url URL --username USER --password PASS --page-size N [--resource-type TYPE]

On success it writes one JSON document to stdout and nothing else, and exits 0:

    {"count": 7, "credentials": [{"id": ..., "username": ..., "accountType": ..., "credentialType": ..., "resourceId": ..., "resourceName": ..., "resourceType": ...}]}

Every credential record carries exactly those seven fields. `id`, `username`, `accountType` and `credentialType` come from the `Credential` itself; `resourceId`, `resourceName` and `resourceType` come from its nested `resource`. The credential passwords the API hands back must never reach the output, and neither must the access token. `credentials` is ordered ascending by `resourceName`, then `username`, then `id`, so the same inventory always emits identically.

`docs/contract.json` is the authoritative wire contract: the `createToken` and `getCredentials` operations projected out of the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0.0.0 SDDC Manager OpenAPI specification pinned in `docs/official_sources.json`. Use those two operations and nothing else, and read paths, methods, query parameters and accepted values out of the contract rather than restating them in code.

The workflow is: POST the supplied username and password to `createToken` for a `TokenPair`, then walk `getCredentials` from `pageNumber` 0 until `pageMetadata.totalPages` is exhausted, collecting every element on the way. Retrieve the collection completely and request no page beyond it. Two details of the 9.0.0.0 page shape matter here: `pageMetadata.pageSize` reports the number of elements in the page that came back rather than the size you asked for, and `elements` is absent rather than empty when a page holds nothing. Honour the caller's `--page-size` on every request instead of collapsing the walk into one oversized page.

Preserve the wire shape the contract defines. `createToken` is unauthenticated, sends `application/json`, and must project only the supplied username and password into `TokenCreationSpec`: `apiKey` and `idToken` were never supplied, so they must be absent, not `null` and not `""`. Every `getCredentials` request carries `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and no body. Query parameters the caller did not supply must be left out of the URL entirely - a trailing `resourceName=` is a protocol error, not a harmless no-op. When `--resource-type` is given it travels as the `resourceType` query parameter; when it is not, that parameter does not appear at all. A `--resource-type` value this API version does not document must be rejected before any request is sent. When the service returns an error response, stop, report it clearly including the status code, and exit non-zero.

`python3 -B tests/verify.py` is the offline acceptance command. It starts a loopback SDDC Manager built from the pinned contract, drives the CLI against it, and asserts both the emitted document and the exact request log the server recorded. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Leave the protected `docs/` and `tests/` files unchanged.
